title: Localizations of N-1 and N-2 domains
statement: Let $R$ be an integral domain with field of fractions $K$ and $S\subseteq R$ a multiplicative subset ($1\in S$, $st\in S$ for $s,t\in S$) with $0\notin S$, and let $S^{-1}R$ be the localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Then $S^{-1}R$ is an integral domain, and the map $S^{-1}R\to K$, $r/s\mapsto r/s$, is injective and identifies $K$ with the field of fractions of $S^{-1}R$. Moreover: (1) if $R$ is N-1 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain], then $S^{-1}R$ is N-1; (2) if $R$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain], then $S^{-1}R$ is N-2.
